bo-nuong-ong-tre.name: Bamboo Tube Grilled Beef
bo-nuong-ong-tre.serving_basis: Four portions for a Vietnamese family meal.
bo-nuong-ong-tre.description: Beef shank with a little brisket fat is marinated with lemongrass, ginger, and mắc khén, then grilled inside a bamboo tube. The enclosed heat keeps the meat moist and carries the fragrance of bamboo and highland spices.
bo-nuong-ong-tre.finished_dish: The beef is evenly cooked, moist, lightly charred at the edges, and fragrant with lemongrass, ginger, and mắc khén; the center is fully cooked.
bo-nuong-ong-tre.serving: Remove the beef from the tube and serve hot with cơm lam or sticky rice, cucumber, and herbs. Serve mắc khén salt on the side.
tips: Do not pack the meat tightly; leave space at the opening for steam to circulate.
Rotate the tube over the coals so one area does not burn.
Open the tube carefully while hot and check the thickest piece; cook longer if the center is pink.
bo-nuong-ong-tre.image_alt: Beef grilled in a fresh bamboo tube with lemongrass, ginger, and mắc khén.
bo-nuong-ong-tre.media_alt_text: Beef grilled in a fresh bamboo tube with lemongrass, ginger, and mắc khén.
bo-nuong-ong-tre.time_note: About 1 hour 25 minutes; grilling time varies with tube size and the heat of the coals.

ingredients.name: Beef shank with a little brisket fat
ingredients.notes: Cut into 2 cm pieces and pat dry.

ingredients.name: Fresh bamboo tubes
ingredients.notes: About 5–7 cm wide, with one closed end; scrub and rinse with boiling water.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Finely chopped.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Minced; reduce for a milder dish.

ingredients.name: Mắc khén pepper
ingredients.notes: Lightly toasted and ground.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to its saltiness.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use as a starting amount.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the marinade.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Mix into the marinade.

ingredients.name: Banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinsed and rolled into plugs for the tube openings.

preparation_steps: Pat the beef dry and cut it into even pieces about 2 cm wide.
Mince the lemongrass, ginger, shallot, garlic, and chili. Toast and grind the mắc khén.
Mix the beef with the aromatics, seasonings, and oil; marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Scrub the bamboo tubes, rinse with boiling water, and drain. Rinse the banana leaves for the plugs.
cooking_steps: Fill each tube loosely, leaving 3–4 cm at the opening, and plug it with banana leaf.
Set the tubes at an angle over steady glowing coals. Rotate every 5–7 minutes and grill for about 40–45 minutes.
Let the tubes cool briefly before opening. Check the thickest piece; grill longer if the center is still pink.

canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.name: Squash Blossom Soup with Shrimp and Enoki
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.serving_basis: A pot of soup for four people to share.
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.description: Yellow squash blossoms are filled with shrimp and pork paste, then simmered with whole shrimp and enoki mushrooms in a light broth. Add the mushrooms and blossoms near the end to preserve their color and texture.
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.finished_dish: The blossoms are tender but still yellow, the shrimp and pork filling is set, the shrimp taste sweet, and the enoki remain delicate in a clear, mild broth.
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.serving: Ladle into bowls while hot and finish with cilantro. Serve with steamed rice and a braised or stir-fried dish.
tips: Remove the stamens and keep the tender stem so each blossom stays intact for filling.
Mix the filling until cohesive and stuff gently to avoid tearing the petals.
Cook the blossoms just until tender; avoid a long simmer that darkens them.
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.image_alt: A bowl of clear squash blossom soup with shrimp, pork filling, enoki mushrooms, and cilantro.
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.media_alt_text: A bowl of clear squash blossom soup with shrimp, pork filling, enoki mushrooms, and cilantro.
canh-bong-bi-tom-nam-kim-cham.time_note: About 40 minutes, including shrimp preparation, filling the blossoms, and cooking the soup.

ingredients.name: Squash blossoms
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh buds; remove the stamens and rinse gently.

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel and devein; mince 100 g for the filling and leave the rest whole.

ingredients.name: Pork paste
ingredients.notes: Keep chilled until ready to mix.

ingredients.name: Enoki mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the root, rinse quickly, and separate into small clusters.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinsed and chopped for the finish.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For a family-sized pot of soup.

ingredients.name: Rock sugar
ingredients.notes: Adds gentle sweetness.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Add gradually.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season after the filling and shrimp are cooked.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For cleaning shrimp and seasoning.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: For the filling.

preparation_steps: Trim tough stems and stamens from the blossoms, leaving about 5 cm of tender stem. Rinse gently.
Trim the mushroom root, rinse quickly, and separate into small clusters. Peel, devein, and drain the shrimp.
Mince 100 g shrimp with shallot, pepper, and a little seasoning powder; combine with the pork paste.
Gently fill each blossom without packing it tightly.
cooking_steps: Bring the water and rock sugar to a boil, then add the whole shrimp and filled blossoms.
Simmer until the shrimp turn pink and the filling is cooked through; skim any foam for a clear broth.
Add the enoki and cook for about 1 minute. Season with fish sauce and seasoning powder.
Turn off the heat as soon as the blossoms are tender. Finish with cilantro and serve.

cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.name: Dill Fried Knifefish Cakes
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.serving_basis: About eight small patties for four diners.
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.description: Knifefish paste is kneaded with minced pork, dill, shallot, and garlic, then fried as small patties. The browned surface is fragrant, while the center stays springy and tender.
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.finished_dish: The fish cakes are evenly golden and drained, with a springy cooked center and a clear aroma of dill and aromatics.
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, boiled vegetables, and chili fish sauce or chili sauce.
tips: Keep the fish and pork chilled before mixing so the paste binds well.
Knead until the mixture is tacky, and keep the patties fairly thin.
Fry over medium heat so the outside browns while the center cooks through.
suggested_pairings: Minced pork and rau ngót soup
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.image_alt: Golden knifefish patties mixed with dill on a blue-and-white ceramic plate.
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.media_alt_text: Golden knifefish patties mixed with dill on a blue-and-white ceramic plate.
cha-ca-thac-lac-chien-thi-la.time_note: About 45 minutes; fry in batches so the oil temperature stays steady.

suggested_pairings: Minced pork and rau ngót soup

ingredients.name: Knifefish paste
ingredients.notes: Keep chilled and pat dry if watery.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: Choose pork with a little fat to keep the cakes moist.

ingredients.name: Dill
ingredients.notes: Rinsed and finely chopped.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Rinsed and chopped.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the paste and sauce.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use as a starting amount.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the mixture gradually.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Reduce for young children.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For shallow frying; the patties absorb less than the amount in the pan.

preparation_steps: Keep the fish and ground pork chilled. Rinse the dill and scallions, then chop them; mince the shallot and garlic.
Mix the knifefish paste with pork, shallot, garlic, fish sauce, seasoning powder, salt, and pepper.
Knead until tacky, then fold in the dill and scallions.
cooking_steps: Lightly oil your hands, divide the mixture evenly, and shape into moderately thin patties.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Fry in batches, turning when the edges set and begin to brown.
Cook until both sides are golden and the centers are fully cooked; drain on paper towels.

ca-lo-o-kho-mang.name: Lồ Ồ Fish Braised with Sour Bamboo Shoots
aliases: Lồ Ồ Fish with Bamboo Shoots
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.serving_basis: A pot of braised fish for four people to share with rice.
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.description: Firm cá lồ ồ is lightly fried and slowly braised with sour bamboo shoots, shallot, garlic, and chili. The savory glaze clings to the fish, while the bamboo shoots add a gentle tang to the meal.
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.finished_dish: The fish is firm and seasoned but still in intact pieces; the bamboo shoots are tender-crisp and the sauce is lightly reduced with balanced salty, sweet, sour, and spicy notes.
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a mild boiled vegetable or soup to balance the braise.
tips: Briefly boil the bamboo shoots if their sourness is sharp; drain well so the sauce does not become thin.
Sear the fish just until the surface firms, then avoid turning it repeatedly.
Taste the braising liquid before it reduces because bamboo shoots and fish sauce vary in salt and sourness.
search_terms: cá lồ ồ braised with bamboo shoots
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.image_alt: Whole cá lồ ồ fish braised with sour bamboo shoots, chili, and amber sauce in a clay pot.
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.media_alt_text: Whole cá lồ ồ fish braised with sour bamboo shoots, chili, and amber sauce in a clay pot.
ca-lo-o-kho-mang.time_note: About 45 minutes, not including soaking or parboiling the bamboo shoots to reduce sourness.

ingredients.name: Cá lồ ồ fish
ingredients.notes: Clean, remove the gills and innards, and score lightly.

ingredients.name: Sour bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Rinse and briefly boil if the flavor is very sharp, then drain.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Slice; remove seeds for less heat.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to its saltiness.

ingredients.name: Rice vinegar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the sourness of the bamboo shoots.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the sour and salty flavors.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use as a starting amount.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For preparing and seasoning the fish.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: For the marinade.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For searing the fish; adjust to the pan.

ingredients.name: Hot water
ingredients.notes: Mix with the remaining marinade for braising.

preparation_steps: Clean and drain the fish, then score it lightly. Rinse the sour bamboo shoots and briefly boil if needed.
Mince the shallot and garlic and slice the chili. Marinate the fish for about 10 minutes with some fish sauce, vinegar, sugar, pepper, and salt.
cooking_steps: Heat a shallow layer of oil and briefly fry the fish until the surface firms; remove and drain.
Use a little of the oil to fry the shallot and garlic until fragrant. Add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry for about 3 minutes.
Transfer the shoots to a pot and arrange the fish on top. Mix the remaining seasonings with hot water, pour them in, cover, and simmer gently for about 15 minutes.
Carefully turn the fish and braise for about 15 minutes more, until cooked and lightly glazed with the sauce.

dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.name: Vegetarian Okra Stir-Fry with Tomatoes
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.serving_basis: A vegetable side dish for four people at a family meal.
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.description: Green okra is briefly blanched and then stir-fried with ripe tomatoes. Their gentle tang forms a light sauce, making this an easy vegetarian dish to serve with rice.
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.finished_dish: The okra is tender yet still slightly crisp, while the tomatoes soften into a light, tangy sauce. The seasoning is balanced and not overpowering.
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and other vegetarian dishes.
tips: Blanch the okra for about 3 minutes, then drain it so it finishes quickly in the pan and keeps its green color.
Avoid over-blanching; stir gently after adding the okra so it does not become mushy.
Season gradually, adjusting for the tomatoes’ acidity.
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.image_alt: A plate of green okra stir-fried with softened tomatoes in a light red sauce.
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.media_alt_text: A plate of green okra stir-fried with softened tomatoes in a light red sauce.
dau-bap-xao-ca-chua-chay.time_note: About 25 minutes, including preparation and blanching the okra.

ingredients.name: Okra
ingredients.notes: Choose young pods, rinse, and trim the stems.

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into wedges; choose ripe but firm tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the garlic and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Check the label to ensure it is suitable for a vegetarian meal.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually to taste.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Add at the end or omit if preferred.

preparation_steps: Rinse the okra, trim the stems, and blanch it in boiling water for about 3 minutes. Drain and cut into bite-size pieces.
Rinse the tomatoes and cut them into wedges. Peel and mince the garlic.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and cook until softened and juicy.
Add the blanched okra, vegetarian seasoning, and salt. Stir gently for about 4–5 minutes so the vegetables take on the sauce without breaking apart.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, add black pepper if using, and turn off the heat once the okra is just cooked.
